subject: maths
title: Primary 3 Multiplication and Division
seo_title: P3 Multiplication and Division Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Division with remainder; multiplication and division algorithms (up to 3 digits by 1 digit)
meta_desc: Free P3 practice: multiply and divide up to 3 digits by 1 digit, renaming, remainders and bar model word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Work one place at a time and rename what is left; a remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
body_html:
Multiply with renaming

Start with the ones. If a product is 10 or more, write the ones digit and rename the tens. Add the renamed digit after you multiply the next place.

3-digit × 1-digit

Find the value of 236 × 4.

6 × 4 = 24: write 4, rename 2 tens. 3 × 4 + 2 = 14 tens: write 4, rename 1 hundred. 2 × 4 + 1 = 9 hundreds.

Answer: 944

Division with remainder

Division puts a total into equal groups. What is left over is the remainder. We write it with R. The remainder is always smaller than the divisor.

Long division

Start with the biggest place on the left. Share it, write the answer on top, and rename what is left as the next place.

What the remainder means

In a word problem, read the question and decide what to do with the remainder.

The question asksDo thisExample
Everyone or everything must fitRound up: add 134 pupils, 4 per kayak: 9 kayaks
How many full boxes or groups?Leave the remainder out30 kueh, boxes of 8: 3 boxes
How many are left over?The remainder is the answer35 sweets, 4 friends: 3 left

Word problems with a bar model

Sharing

Mrs Ng shares 252 stickers equally among 7 pupils. How many does each pupil get?

7 units = 252. 1 unit = 252 ÷ 7 = 36.

Answer: 36 stickers

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not adding the renamed digit (47 × 6 = 242)Add the renamed 4 tens: 24 + 4 = 28 tens, so 282
A remainder bigger than the divisor (30 ÷ 4 = 6 R 6)If the remainder is 4 or more, make one more group: 7 R 2
Ignoring the remainder (47 ÷ 5 = 9)Write what is left: 47 ÷ 5 = 9 R 2
Not renaming (72 ÷ 4 = 10)Rename the 3 tens left as 30 ones: 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so 18
34 pupils need 8 kayaks2 pupils are still waiting, so 9 kayaks are needed

faq.q: What multiplication and division is taught in Primary 3 maths?
faq.a: In the MOE syllabus, Primary 3 pupils multiply and divide numbers up to 3 digits by a 1-digit number, such as 236 × 4 and 547 ÷ 4. They also learn division with remainder and the multiplication tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9.

faq.q: How do I explain remainders to my child?
faq.a: Use real objects: put 13 counters into groups of 4 and count what is left. There are 3 groups and 1 left over, so 13 ÷ 4 = 3 R 1, and the remainder is always smaller than 4.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in P3 multiplication and division?
faq.a: Forgetting to add the renamed digit when multiplying is the most common, followed by a remainder that is bigger than the divisor. Checking with quotient × divisor + remainder catches division mistakes.

faq.q: Why do P3 word problems use bar models?
faq.a: A bar model shows equal units, so pupils can see when to multiply and when to divide, for example 3 units = 141, 1 unit = 47. The model method is used all the way to the PSLE in Primary 6.

items.q: Which digit is missing from the answer?
items.e: Work from the ones: 4 ones × 7 = 28, write 8 and rename 2 tens; 6 tens × 7 + 2 = 44, write 4 and rename 4 hundreds; 2 hundreds × 7 + 4 = 18. In that column, 2 × 7 + 4 = 18, so the missing digit is 8. 264 × 7 = 1848.

items.q: Find the value of 673 × 9.
items.e: Start with the ones. 3 ones × 9 = 27, write 7 and rename 2 tens; 7 tens × 9 + 2 = 65, write 5 and rename 6 hundreds; 6 hundreds × 9 + 6 = 60. So 673 × 9 = 6057.

items.q: The discs show 3 groups of 26. Find the value of 26 × 3.
items.e: Ones: 3 × 6 ones = 18 ones. Rename 10 ones as 1 ten: 1 ten 8 ones. Tens: 3 × 2 tens = 6 tens, and 6 + 1 = 7 tens. So 26 × 3 = 78.

items.q: Which is equal to 47 × 6?
items.e: Split 47 by place value: 40 + 7. Every part must be multiplied by 6: 240 + 42 = 282.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Start with the ones. 7 ones × 6 = 42, write 2 and rename 4 tens; 4 tens × 6 + 4 = 28. So 47 × 6 = 282.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Start with the ones. 9 ones × 3 = 27, write 7 and rename 2 tens; 6 tens × 3 + 2 = 20. So 69 × 3 = 207.

items.q: Find the value of 236 × 4.
items.e: Start with the ones. 6 ones × 4 = 24, write 4 and rename 2 tens; 3 tens × 4 + 2 = 14, write 4 and rename 1 hundred; 2 hundreds × 4 + 1 = 9. So 236 × 4 = 944.

items.q: Ryan worked out 49 × 6 like this. What mistake did he make?
c: Did not add the renamed digit
items.e: Ryan wrote each product in full (24, 54) instead of renaming the tens into the next column. Correct: 9 ones × 6 = 54, write 4 and rename 5 tens; 4 tens × 6 + 5 = 29. So 49 × 6 = 294.

items.q: Find the value of 347 × 5.
items.e: Start with the ones. 7 ones × 5 = 35, write 5 and rename 3 tens; 4 tens × 5 + 3 = 23, write 3 and rename 2 hundreds; 3 hundreds × 5 + 2 = 17. So 347 × 5 = 1735.

items.q: Which digit is missing from the answer?
items.e: Work from the ones: 7 ones × 8 = 56, write 6 and rename 5 tens; 5 tens × 8 + 5 = 45. In that column, 5 × 8 + 5 = 45, so the missing digit is 5. 57 × 8 = 456.

items.q: Jun Jie worked out 68 × 7 like this. What mistake did he make?
c: Did not add the renamed digit
items.e: Jun Jie wrote the ones digit of each product but did not add the renamed digit. Correct: 8 ones × 7 = 56, write 6 and rename 5 tens; 6 tens × 7 + 5 = 47. So 68 × 7 = 476.

items.q: Farah worked out 256 × 3 like this. What mistake did she make?
c: Did not add the renamed digit
items.e: Farah added the renamed digit first: (5 + 1) × 3. Multiply first, then add: 5 × 3 + 1. Correct: 6 ones × 3 = 18, write 8 and rename 1 ten; 5 tens × 3 + 1 = 16, write 6 and rename 1 hundred; 2 hundreds × 3 + 1 = 7. So 256 × 3 = 768.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Start with the ones. 8 ones × 6 = 48, write 8 and rename 4 tens; 5 tens × 6 + 4 = 34, write 4 and rename 3 hundreds; 1 hundred × 6 + 3 = 9. So 158 × 6 = 948.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Start with the ones. 8 ones × 9 = 72, write 2 and rename 7 tens; 5 tens × 9 + 7 = 52. So 58 × 9 = 522.

items.q: Find the value of 38 × 4.
items.e: Start with the ones. 8 ones × 4 = 32, write 2 and rename 3 tens; 3 tens × 4 + 3 = 15. So 38 × 4 = 152.

items.q: Find the value of 60 × 7.
items.e: 6 tens × 7 = 42 tens = 420. Think of the fact 6 × 7 = 42, then add the 0 for tens.

items.q: Which is equal to 325 × 4?
items.e: Split 325 by place value: 300 + 20 + 5. Every part must be multiplied by 4: 1200 + 80 + 20 = 1300.

items.q: Find the value of 74 × 8.
items.e: Start with the ones. 4 ones × 8 = 32, write 2 and rename 3 tens; 7 tens × 8 + 3 = 59. So 74 × 8 = 592.

items.q: Find the value of 86 × 7.
items.e: Start with the ones. 6 ones × 7 = 42, write 2 and rename 4 tens; 8 tens × 7 + 4 = 60. So 86 × 7 = 602.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Start with the ones. 9 ones × 7 = 63, write 3 and rename 6 tens; 6 tens × 7 + 6 = 48, write 8 and rename 4 hundreds; 4 hundreds × 7 + 4 = 32. So 469 × 7 = 3283.

items.q: Find the value of 58 ÷ 9.
items.e: Use the multiplication table of 9. 6 × 9 = 54 is the biggest product not more than 58. 58 − 54 = 4 left over. So 58 ÷ 9 = 6 R 4. Check: 6 × 9 + 4 = 58.

items.q: Devi says 30 ÷ 4 = 6 R 6. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The remainder must be smaller than the divisor. 6 is bigger than 4, so one more group of 4 fits. 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2. Check: 7 × 4 + 2 = 30.

items.q: What is the remainder when 38 is divided by 7?
items.e: 5 × 7 = 35, and 38 − 35 = 3. So 38 ÷ 7 = 5 R 3. The question asks for the remainder: 3.

items.q: The picture shows how 25 marbles are put into bags of 4. How many marbles are left over?
items.e: 25 ÷ 4 = 6 R 1. There are 6 full bags and 1 left over (in red).

items.q: Find the value of 44 ÷ 7.
items.e: Use the multiplication table of 7. 6 × 7 = 42 is the biggest product not more than 44. 44 − 42 = 2 left over. So 44 ÷ 7 = 6 R 2. Check: 6 × 7 + 2 = 44.

items.q: The picture shows 23 counters in groups of 5. Find the value of 23 ÷ 5.
items.e: There are 4 groups of 5 and 3 counters left over (in red). 3 is less than 5, so it cannot make another group. 23 ÷ 5 = 4 R 3. Check: 4 × 5 + 3 = 23.

items.q: Which division does the picture show?
items.e: 27 counters make 5 groups of 5, with 2 left over. So 27 ÷ 5 = 5 R 2. Check: 5 × 5 + 2 = 27.

items.q: What is the remainder when 29 is divided by 6?
items.e: 4 × 6 = 24, and 29 − 24 = 5. So 29 ÷ 6 = 4 R 5. The question asks for the remainder: 5.

items.q: The picture shows 13 counters in groups of 4. Find the value of 13 ÷ 4.
items.e: There are 3 groups of 4 and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 4, so it cannot make another group. 13 ÷ 4 = 3 R 1. Check: 3 × 4 + 1 = 13.

items.q: Which division does the picture show?
items.e: 14 counters make 4 groups of 3, with 2 left over. So 14 ÷ 3 = 4 R 2. Check: 4 × 3 + 2 = 14.

items.q: In a division, the quotient is 7, the divisor is 5 and the remainder is 2. What number was divided?
items.e: Work backwards: multiply, then add the remainder. 7 × 5 = 35, and 35 + 2 = 37. Check: 37 ÷ 5 = 7 R 2.

items.q: The picture shows 22 counters in groups of 3. Find the value of 22 ÷ 3.
items.e: There are 7 groups of 3 and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 3, so it cannot make another group. 22 ÷ 3 = 7 R 1. Check: 7 × 3 + 1 = 22.

items.q: The picture shows 26 counters in groups of 4. Find the value of 26 ÷ 4.
items.e: There are 6 groups of 4 and 2 counters left over (in red). 2 is less than 4, so it cannot make another group. 26 ÷ 4 = 6 R 2. Check: 6 × 4 + 2 = 26.

items.q: The picture shows 19 counters in groups of 6. Find the value of 19 ÷ 6.
items.e: There are 3 groups of 6 and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 6, so it cannot make another group. 19 ÷ 6 = 3 R 1. Check: 3 × 6 + 1 = 19.

items.q: What is the remainder when 50 is divided by 8?
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48, and 50 − 48 = 2. So 50 ÷ 8 = 6 R 2. The question asks for the remainder: 2.

items.q: Find the value of 35 ÷ 8.
items.e: Use the multiplication table of 8. 4 × 8 = 32 is the biggest product not more than 35. 35 − 32 = 3 left over. So 35 ÷ 8 = 4 R 3. Check: 4 × 8 + 3 = 35.

items.q: The picture shows 31 counters in groups of 6. Find the value of 31 ÷ 6.
items.e: There are 5 groups of 6 and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 6, so it cannot make another group. 31 ÷ 6 = 5 R 1. Check: 5 × 6 + 1 = 31.

items.q: The picture shows how 20 buttons are put into bags of 6. How many buttons are left over?
items.e: 20 ÷ 6 = 3 R 2. There are 3 full bags and 2 left over (in red).

items.q: You divide a number by 4. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always smaller than the divisor. When you divide by 4, the remainder can only be 0, 1, 2 or 3.

items.q: The picture shows 17 counters in groups of 5. Find the value of 17 ÷ 5.
items.e: There are 3 groups of 5 and 2 counters left over (in red). 2 is less than 5, so it cannot make another group. 17 ÷ 5 = 3 R 2. Check: 3 × 5 + 2 = 17.

items.q: Find the value of 293 ÷ 5.
items.e: 2 hundreds ÷ 5: not enough to share. Rename as 20 tens: 29 tens. 29 tens ÷ 5 = 5 tens, 4 tens left. Rename 4 tens as 40 ones: 43 ones. 43 ones ÷ 5 = 8 R 3. Answer: 58 R 3. Check: 58 × 5 + 3 = 293.

items.q: The place-value discs show 348. Share them equally into 3 groups. What number is in each group?
items.e: 3 hundreds ÷ 3 = 1 hundred. 4 tens ÷ 3 = 1 ten, 1 ten left. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 18 ones. 18 ones ÷ 3 = 6 ones. Answer: 116. Check: 116 × 3 = 348.

items.q: Find the value of 96 ÷ 8.
items.e: 9 tens ÷ 8 = 1 ten, 1 ten left. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 16 ones. 16 ones ÷ 8 = 2 ones. Answer: 12. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 6 hundreds ÷ 7: not enough to share. Rename as 60 tens: 67 tens. 67 tens ÷ 7 = 9 tens, 4 tens left. Rename 4 tens as 40 ones: 42 ones. 42 ones ÷ 7 = 6 ones. Answer: 96. Check: 96 × 7 = 672.

items.q: How many digits does the answer to 256 ÷ 8 have?
items.e: 2 hundreds ÷ 8: not enough to share, so there are no hundreds in the answer. Rename as 20 tens: 25 tens. 25 tens ÷ 8 = 3 tens, 1 ten left. Rename as 10 ones: 16 ones. 16 ÷ 8 = 2. 256 ÷ 8 = 32, which has 2 digits.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 8 tens ÷ 5 = 1 ten, 3 tens left. Rename 3 tens as 30 ones: 37 ones. 37 ones ÷ 5 = 7 R 2. Answer: 17 R 2. Check: 17 × 5 + 2 = 87.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 8 hundreds ÷ 6 = 1 hundred, 2 hundreds left. Rename 2 hundreds as 20 tens: 23 tens. 23 tens ÷ 6 = 3 tens, 5 tens left. Rename 5 tens as 50 ones: 55 ones. 55 ones ÷ 6 = 9 R 1. Answer: 139 R 1. Check: 139 × 6 + 1 = 835.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 7 tens ÷ 4 = 1 ten, 3 tens left. Rename 3 tens as 30 ones: 32 ones. 32 ones ÷ 4 = 8 ones. Answer: 18. Check: 18 × 4 = 72.

items.q: Find the value of 65 ÷ 4.
items.e: 6 tens ÷ 4 = 1 ten, 2 tens left. Rename 2 tens as 20 ones: 25 ones. 25 ones ÷ 4 = 6 R 1. Answer: 16 R 1. Check: 16 × 4 + 1 = 65.

items.q: Find the value of 547 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 hundreds ÷ 4 = 1 hundred, 1 hundred left. Rename 1 hundred as 10 tens: 14 tens. 14 tens ÷ 4 = 3 tens, 2 tens left. Rename 2 tens as 20 ones: 27 ones. 27 ones ÷ 4 = 6 R 3. Answer: 136 R 3. Check: 136 × 4 + 3 = 547.

items.q: Find the value of 75 ÷ 3.
items.e: 7 tens ÷ 3 = 2 tens, 1 ten left. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 15 ones. 15 ones ÷ 3 = 5 ones. Answer: 25. Check: 25 × 3 = 75.

items.q: Which division has no remainder?
Which multiplication checks that 952 ÷ 7 = 136?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the number you divided by: 136 × 7 = 952. That is the number you started with, so the answer is correct.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 5 hundreds ÷ 4 = 1 hundred, 1 hundred left. Rename 1 hundred as 10 tens: 13 tens. 13 tens ÷ 4 = 3 tens, 1 ten left. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 16 ones. 16 ones ÷ 4 = 4 ones. Answer: 134. Check: 134 × 4 = 536.

items.q: The place-value discs show 156. Share them equally into 3 groups. What number is in each group?
items.e: 1 hundred ÷ 3: not enough to share. Rename as 10 tens: 15 tens. 15 tens ÷ 3 = 5 tens. 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones. Answer: 52. Check: 52 × 3 = 156.

items.q: To find 75 ÷ 3, Kavya writes 7 tens ÷ 3 = 2 tens, with 1 ten left. What should she do with the 1 ten?
items.e: The 1 ten left over must still be shared. Rename it as 10 ones: 10 + 5 = 15 ones. 15 ones ÷ 3 = 5 ones. So 75 ÷ 3 = 25.

items.q: Siti says 618 ÷ 6 = 13. What mistake did she make?
c: She left out the 0 in the tens place
items.e: 6 hundreds ÷ 6 = 1 hundred. 1 ten ÷ 6 = 0: write 0 in the tens place. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 18 ones. 18 ones ÷ 6 = 3 ones. The answer is 103, not 13. Check: 103 × 6 = 618.

items.q: Find the value of 424 ÷ 8.
items.e: 4 hundreds ÷ 8: not enough to share. Rename as 40 tens: 42 tens. 42 tens ÷ 8 = 5 tens, 2 tens left. Rename 2 tens as 20 ones: 24 ones. 24 ones ÷ 8 = 3 ones. Answer: 53. Check: 53 × 8 = 424.

items.q: Find the value of 918 ÷ 6.
items.e: 9 hundreds ÷ 6 = 1 hundred, 3 hundreds left. Rename 3 hundreds as 30 tens: 31 tens. 31 tens ÷ 6 = 5 tens, 1 ten left. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 18 ones. 18 ones ÷ 6 = 3 ones. Answer: 153. Check: 153 × 6 = 918.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 8 tens ÷ 6 = 1 ten, 2 tens left. Rename 2 tens as 20 ones: 24 ones. 24 ones ÷ 6 = 4 ones. Answer: 14. Check: 14 × 6 = 84.

items.q: Wei Ming has 27 stickers. He makes rows of 6 stickers. How many full rows can he make?
items.e: 27 ÷ 6 = 4 R 3. The 3 stickers left over cannot make another full row. Leave the remainder out: the answer is 4 rows.

items.q: A ribbon is 75 cm long. Hui Min cuts it into pieces of 9 cm. How many 9 cm pieces can she cut?
items.e: 75 ÷ 9 = 8 R 3. The 3 cm left over is too short for another piece. Leave the remainder out: the answer is 8 pieces.

items.q: 29 pupils sit at tables of 4. 29 ÷ 4 = 7 R 1. What does the 1 mean?
items.e: 7 tables of 4 seat 28 pupils. 29 − 28 = 1, so 1 pupil still needs a seat. The remainder tells you what is left over.

items.q: Sarah says 47 ÷ 5 = 9. What mistake did she make?
items.e: 9 × 5 = 45, and 47 − 45 = 2. The 2 left over is part of the answer: 47 ÷ 5 = 9 R 2.

items.q: In which story should you round up to the next whole number?
c: Buns left when 50 go on 6 trays
items.e: 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2. With 7 boats, 2 pupils still need a place, so you need 8 boats. Round up when everyone must fit.

items.q: Ahmad puts 23 eggs into boxes of 6. How many eggs are left over?
items.e: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 R 5 (3 × 6 = 18, 23 − 18 = 5). The question asks how many are left over, so the answer is the remainder: 5 eggs.

items.q: Ryan has $50. A storybook costs $8. He buys as many as he can. How much money does he have left?
items.e: 50 ÷ 8 = 6 R 2. 6 books cost 6 × $8 = $48. $50 − $48 = $2. He has $2 left. ($6 is the number of books, not the money.)

items.q: Jun Jie has $40. A movie ticket costs $7. How many tickets can he buy?
items.e: 40 ÷ 7 = 5 R 5. 5 tickets cost $35. The $5 left over is not enough for another ticket. Leave the remainder out: the answer is 5 tickets.

items.q: 34 pupils go kayaking at East Coast Park. Each kayak holds 4 pupils. How many kayaks are needed?
items.e: 34 ÷ 4 = 8 R 2. 8 kayaks are not enough: 2 pupils still need a place. Round up to 9 kayaks.

items.q: Mrs Lim has 22 pencils. A pencil case holds 5 pencils. How many pencil cases does she need for all the pencils?
items.e: 22 ÷ 5 = 4 R 2. 4 pencil cases are not enough: 2 pencils still need a place. Round up to 5 pencil cases.

items.q: Farah has 45 photos for an album. Each page holds 6 photos. How many pages does she need for all of them?
items.e: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 R 3. 7 pages are not enough: 3 photos still need a place. Round up to 8 pages.

items.q: Mdm Wong bakes 30 kueh. She packs them in boxes of 8. How many boxes can she fill?
items.e: 30 ÷ 8 = 3 R 6. The 6 kueh left over cannot fill another box. Leave the remainder out: the answer is 3 boxes.

items.q: 56 pupils go on a trip. Each van holds 9 pupils. Siti says 6 vans are needed. Ali says 7 vans are needed. Who is correct?
c: Ali, because 2 pupils still need a place
items.e: 56 ÷ 9 = 6 R 2. 6 vans hold 54 pupils, and 2 pupils still need a place. So 7 vans are needed. Ali is correct.

items.q: A fruit seller packs 92 rambutans into bags of 8. How many full bags does she get?
items.e: 92 ÷ 8 = 11 R 4. The 4 rambutans left over cannot fill another bag. Leave the remainder out: the answer is 11 bags.

items.q: Mr Tan needs to carry 50 chairs to the hall. He can carry 3 chairs on each trip. How many trips must he make?
items.e: 50 ÷ 3 = 16 R 2. 16 trips are not enough: 2 chairs still need a place. Round up to 17 trips.

items.q: A teacher puts 58 books on shelves. Each shelf holds 9 books. How many books are left over after the shelves are full?
items.e: 58 ÷ 9 = 6 R 4 (6 × 9 = 54, 58 − 54 = 4). The question asks how many are left over, so the answer is the remainder: 4 books.

items.q: There are 39 guests at a Hari Raya open house. Each table seats 4 guests. How many tables are needed?
items.e: 39 ÷ 4 = 9 R 3. 9 tables are not enough: 3 guests still need a place. Round up to 10 tables.

items.q: 93 mandarin oranges are packed into bags of 7 for Chinese New Year. How many oranges are left over?
items.e: 93 ÷ 7 = 13 R 2 (13 × 7 = 91, 93 − 91 = 2). The question asks how many are left over, so the answer is the remainder: 2 oranges.

items.q: Devi shares 35 sweets equally among 4 friends. How many sweets are left over?
items.e: 35 ÷ 4 = 8 R 3 (8 × 4 = 32, 35 − 32 = 3). The question asks how many are left over, so the answer is the remainder: 3 sweets.

items.q: Nurul makes bracelets with 8 beads each. She has 70 beads. How many beads are left over?
items.e: 70 ÷ 8 = 8 R 6 (8 × 8 = 64, 70 − 64 = 6). The question asks how many are left over, so the answer is the remainder: 6 beads.

items.q: Chloe buys 4 bowls of laksa at $6 each. She pays with a $50 note. How much change does she get?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × $6 = $24. Step 2: $50 − $24 = $26. Chloe gets $26 change. ($24 is the cost, not the change.)

items.q: Mdm Wong bakes 144 cupcakes for Children’s Day. She puts 6 cupcakes in each box. How many boxes does she fill?
items.e: Find how many 6s are in 144: 144 ÷ 6. 1 hundred ÷ 6: not enough to share. Rename as 10 tens: 14 tens. 14 tens ÷ 6 = 2 tens, 2 tens left. Rename 2 tens as 20 ones: 24 ones. 24 ones ÷ 6 = 4 ones. Answer: 24 boxes. (144 × 6 = 864 multiplies instead of dividing.) Check: 24 × 6 = 144.

items.q: A box has 128 crayons. How many crayons are there in 6 boxes?
items.e: 6 units of 128. 128 × 6: 8 ones × 6 = 48, write 8 and rename 4 tens; 2 tens × 6 + 4 = 16, write 6 and rename 1 hundred; 1 hundred × 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 768 crayons.

items.q: A shop sold 136 cups of bubble tea on Monday. On Tuesday it sold twice as many cups. How many cups did it sell on the two days altogether?
items.e: Monday is 1 unit and Tuesday is 2 units: 3 units altogether. 136 × 3 = 408 cups. (272 is Tuesday only, and 398 forgets the renamed ten.) Check: 136 + 272 = 408.

items.q: A packet of rice weighs 5 kg. How many kilograms do 136 packets weigh?
items.e: Multiply: 136 × 5. 6 ones × 5 = 30, write 0 and rename 3 tens; 3 tens × 5 + 3 = 18, write 8 and rename 1 hundred; 1 hundred × 5 + 1 = 6. Answer: 680 kg.

items.q: Zhi Hao has 4 times as many cards as Hafiz. They have 245 cards altogether. How many cards does Hafiz have?
items.e: Hafiz has 1 unit and Zhi Hao has 4 units, so 5 units = 245. 1 unit = 245 ÷ 5 = 49. Hafiz has 49 cards. (245 ÷ 4 = 61 R 1 forgets Hafiz’s unit, and 980 multiplies instead of dividing.) Check: 49 × 5 = 245.

items.q: Ali has 47 marbles. Siti has 3 times as many marbles as Ali. How many marbles does Siti have?
items.e: Siti has 3 units. 1 unit = 47. 3 units = 47 × 3 = 141 (7 × 3 = 21, write 1 and rename 2 tens; 4 tens × 3 + 2 = 14 tens). Siti has 141 marbles. (47 + 3 = 50 adds instead of multiplying.)

items.q: 312 pupils are put into 6 equal teams for Sports Day. Which number sentence finds the number of pupils in each team?
items.e: You know the total (312) and the number of teams (6), so divide: 312 ÷ 6 = 52. 6 ÷ 312 divides the wrong way. Check: 52 × 6 = 312.

items.q: Mrs Lim packs 38 goodie bags for Children’s Day. A carton holds 5 goodie bags. How many cartons does she need to pack all the bags?
items.e: 38 ÷ 5 = 7 R 3. 7 cartons are not enough: 3 goodie bags still need a place. Round up to 8 cartons.

items.q: Mrs Lim buys 6 packets of 24 rambutans. She shares them equally among 8 neighbours. How many rambutans does each neighbour get?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 24 = 144 rambutans. Step 2: 144 ÷ 8 = 18 (14 tens ÷ 8 = 1 ten, 6 tens left; rename as 60 ones: 64 ones; 64 ÷ 8 = 8). Each neighbour gets 18 rambutans.

items.q: Priya has 36 stamps. Ethan has 5 times as many stamps as Priya. How many more stamps does Ethan have than Priya?
items.e: Ethan has 4 more units than Priya. 1 unit = 36, so 4 units = 36 × 4 = 144. (180 is all of Ethan’s stamps.) Check: 36 × 5 − 36 = 180 − 36 = 144.

items.q: Mr Tan had 400 cm of wire. He cut off 4 pieces of 75 cm each. How much wire was left?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × 75 = 300 cm. Step 2: 400 − 300 = 100 cm left. (325 cm takes away only one piece. 120 cm comes from 4 × 75 = 280, which forgets the renamed 2 tens.)

items.q: Mrs Ng shares 252 stickers equally among 7 pupils. How many stickers does each pupil get?
items.e: 7 units = 252, so 1 unit = 252 ÷ 7. 2 hundreds ÷ 7: not enough to share. Rename as 20 tens: 25 tens. 25 tens ÷ 7 = 3 tens, 4 tens left. Rename 4 tens as 40 ones: 42 ones. 42 ones ÷ 7 = 6 ones. Answer: 36 stickers. Check: 36 × 7 = 252.

items.q: A zoo ticket for a child costs $27. Mr Kumar buys 4 tickets for his children. How much does he pay?
items.e: Multiply: 27 × 4. 7 ones × 4 = 28, write 8 and rename 2 tens; 2 tens × 4 + 2 = 10. Answer: $108.

items.q: Raju packs 168 durian puffs equally into 8 boxes. How many durian puffs are in each box?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: 168 ÷ 8. 1 hundred ÷ 8: not enough to share. Rename as 10 tens: 16 tens. 16 tens ÷ 8 = 2 tens. 8 ones ÷ 8 = 1 one. Answer: 21 durian puffs. Check: 21 × 8 = 168.

items.q: A hawker sold 85 plates of prata in the morning and 83 plates in the afternoon. Each plate has 2 pieces of prata. How many pieces of prata did he sell?
items.e: Step 1: 85 + 83 = 168 plates. Step 2: 168 × 2 = 336 pieces (8 × 2 = 16, rename 1 ten; 6 tens × 2 + 1 = 13 tens, rename 1 hundred; 1 hundred × 2 + 1 = 3 hundreds). (226 forgets the renamed digits.)

items.q: Mr Rahman cuts a 345 cm rope into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: 345 ÷ 5. 3 hundreds ÷ 5: not enough to share. Rename as 30 tens: 34 tens. 34 tens ÷ 5 = 6 tens, 4 tens left. Rename 4 tens as 40 ones: 45 ones. 45 ones ÷ 5 = 9 ones. Answer: 69 cm. Check: 69 × 5 = 345.

items.q: Each bus has 45 seats. How many seats are there in 8 buses?
items.e: 8 units of 45. 45 × 8: 5 ones × 8 = 40, write 0 and rename 4 tens; 4 tens × 8 + 4 = 36. Answer: 360 seats.

items.q: Sarah has 100 cm of ribbon. Each bow needs 8 cm. How many bows can she make?
items.e: 100 ÷ 8 = 12 R 4. The 4 cm left over is not enough for another bow. Leave the remainder out: the answer is 12 bows.

items.q: A school canteen sold 96 plates of chicken rice in 4 days. It sold the same number each day. How many plates did it sell each day?
items.e: 4 units = 96, so 1 unit = 96 ÷ 4. 9 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens, 1 ten left. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 16 ones. 16 ones ÷ 4 = 4 ones. Answer: 24 plates. Check: 24 × 4 = 96.
